titleText.es: Excelente recuperación... ¡algo que podríamos usar para salvar a tu primer hermano de alguna manera!
titleText.en: Excellent recovery: ... which we could try to use to somehow save your original brother!
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive and official xkcd source both identify comic #660. The Spanish title text translates the official afterthought while changing “original brother” to primer hermano. The raster restores MURIÓ and CORAZÓN accents and joins the visible line-broken words SENTÍ, ACORDE, and VELOCIDAD.

regions.labelEs: CONSEJOS DE SIMPATÍA PARA LOS FÍSICOS
EN EL MOMENTO EN QUE MURIÓ MI HERMANO, SENTÍ UN DOLOR ABRASADOR EN MI CORAZÓN.

applications.explanationEn: These five words form the time connector: the first en sets the point in time, and en que links that point to the following event.
Abrasador follows dolor in the common neutral order for a descriptive adjective.
Abrasador is masculine singular to match masculine singular dolor.
Lo and siento form the fixed apology; mucho strengthens it but is not required by the shared expression.

regions.labelEs: INCORRECTO: ¿FUE INSTANTÁNEO O HUBO UN RETRASO ACORDE CON LA VELOCIDAD DE LA LUZ?

applications.explanationEn: Acorde describes the delay as matching a physical limit, and con introduces that standard.
Acorde follows retraso and describes the delay before con introduces the standard it matches.
Acorde is singular to match singular retraso and has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns.
Velocidad names the speed, while de la luz identifies light as what travels.

regions.labelEs: MUY INCORRECTO: SI FUE INSTANTÁNEO, CON UNA CIERTA DISPOSICIÓN DE SISTEMAS DE REFERENCIA EN MOVIMIENTO, ¡PODRÍAMOS ENVIAR SEÑALES ATRÁS EN EL TIEMPO Y VIOLAR LA CAUSALIDAD! ¿CUÁNTOS HERMANOS VIVOS TE QUEDAN?

applications.explanationEn: Sistemas is plural, de classifies their role, and referencia supplies the standard technical term.
Cuántos carries a written accent because it directly asks for a quantity.
Vivos follows hermanos in the common neutral order for a descriptive adjective.
Vivos uses masculine plural -os to match masculine plural hermanos.
Quedan is plural because hermanos vivos names more than one possible remaining person, while cuántos asks for the quantity.

cards.noteEn: Consejos is grammatically plural in Spanish even when natural English simply uses the uncountable word “advice.”
Here simpatía is fellow-feeling for someone in pain, not simply friendliness.

example.en: She showed sympathy for the family.

cards.questionEn: Why is a physics discussion an especially inappropriate response to grief here?
cards.answerEn: The joke contrasts the empathy a grieving person needs with physicists who become absorbed in a relativity puzzle about faster-than-light information.
cards.noteEn: Special relativity treats the speed of light as a limit for transmitted information. If a signal were instantaneous in one reference frame, another moving frame could order the events differently, threatening ordinary cause-before-effect causality. The escalating technical excitement ignores the human loss; the official title text extends the absurdity by imagining a way to exploit the discovery.
As a noun, físicos names people who work in physics. The same written form can be an adjective meaning “physical” when it describes a plural masculine noun.
Before a specific moment, en can correspond to English “at.”

example.en: He arrived at just the right moment.

cards.promptEs: en el momento en que + hecho
cards.questionEn: How do you introduce something that happened at the exact moment another event occurred?
cards.answerEn: Use en el momento en que, then state the event.
cards.noteEn: En el momento en que acts as one time connector. En begins the time setting, el momento names the point, and en que links it to the event. The following verb changes normally for the person and time.

example.es: En el momento en que sonó el timbre, salimos.
example.en: The moment the bell rang, we left.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links a time noun to que
cards.noteEn: In a connector such as el momento en que, en que works like “when” or “in which.”

example.es: Recuerdo el día en que llegó.
example.en: I remember the day when she arrived.

cards.noteEn: Que connects a noun to information describing it. Depending on the noun, English translates it as “who,” “that,” or “which.”

example.es: La persona que llamó es mi amiga.
example.en: The person who called is my friend.

cards.noteEn: Murió is the completed past form of morir for one person or thing.

example.es: La planta murió durante el invierno.
example.en: The plant died during the winter.

cards.noteEn: Sentí is the completed-past form of sentir for the speaker. The stem changes from sient- in siento to sent- in sentí.

cards.questionEn: Where does a basic Spanish describing word usually go relative to its noun?
cards.answerEn: Put it after the noun in the common neutral order.
cards.noteEn: Many ordinary descriptive words follow the person or thing they describe: un coche rojo, una casa grande. Some adjectives commonly come before the noun, and moving an adjective can change emphasis or meaning, so this is a useful default rather than an absolute rule.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.noteEn: In a social comparison, correcto can mean appropriate or acceptable rather than factually correct.

example.es: Fue la respuesta correcta para la ocasión.
example.en: It was the appropriate response for the occasion.

cards.answerEn: it (in the fixed apology lo siento, I'm sorry)

cards.noteEn: Use this fixed expression for an apology or when reacting sympathetically to bad news. Learn it as a complete expression instead of translating lo and siento separately.
cards.questionEn: What is the standard way to say “I'm sorry” when apologizing or expressing sympathy?

example.en: I'm sorry. It was a mistake.

cards.answerEn: I feel (in lo siento: I'm sorry)

cards.noteEn: Mucho can stand by itself when the kind of amount is already clear. It then means ‘much’ or ‘a lot’ without a following noun.

cards.answerEn: was (a completed past instance of ser)

cards.noteEn: Hubo is the completed-past impersonal form of haber. It stays singular even when the thing mentioned afterward is plural.
Acorde con introduces the rule, evidence, or standard that something matches.

example.es: La decisión es acorde con las normas.
example.en: The decision is consistent with the rules.

cards.promptEs: acorde con + norma, plan o hecho
cards.questionEn: How do you say that something is consistent with a rule, plan, or fact?
cards.answerEn: Use acorde con before the standard or information that it matches.
cards.noteEn: Acorde changes to acordes when it describes more than one thing; con remains fixed and introduces what provides the comparison.

example.es: Los datos son acordes con la predicción.
example.en: The data are consistent with the prediction.

cards.questionEn: What is the standard Spanish term for the speed at which light travels?
cards.noteEn: Velocidad names speed, and de la luz identifies light as what travels. The phrase is a conventional scientific term and can follow words such as medir, superar, or cerca de.

example.es: Nada viaja más rápido que la velocidad de la luz.
example.en: Nothing travels faster than the speed of light.

cards.questionEn: What Spanish term names the viewpoint or coordinate system from which motion is measured?
cards.answerEn: Use sistema de referencia; use sistemas de referencia for more than one.
cards.noteEn: De referencia classifies the kind of sistema. In physics, changing the reference frame can change measured positions and velocities, while the noun sistema carries the singular or plural ending.

example.es: Medimos la velocidad desde otro sistema de referencia.
example.en: We measured the speed from another reference frame.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links an item to its type
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between an item and the noun that identifies its type. English often puts the type noun first instead: libro de historia becomes “history book.”

cards.answerEn: reference (in sistema de referencia, reference frame)
cards.noteEn: In physics, referencia helps name the coordinate viewpoint from which motion is measured.

example.es: Elegimos un sistema de referencia fijo.
example.en: We chose a fixed reference frame.

cards.answerEn: we could (a possibility or tentative suggestion)
cards.noteEn: Podríamos is the “would/could” form of poder for “we.” Poder keeps its whole dictionary form and adds -íamos. It often makes a suggestion sound tentative rather than stating a firm plan.
Here señales are physical or electronic signals sent from one place or time to another, not signs that serve as evidence.

example.es: La antena envía señales de radio.

cards.answerEn: to violate; to break (a rule or principle)

cards.noteEn: In physics, causality is the principle that an effect cannot occur before the cause that produces it.

example.es: La teoría debe respetar la causalidad.

cards.noteEn: Cuántos carries a written accent in a direct or indirect question and changes to cuántas before a feminine plural noun.

cards.answerEn: Write qué, cómo, cuándo, and similar words with an accent when they ask a question or add an exclamation.
cards.noteEn: This includes direct questions (¿Qué quieres?), questions inside another sentence (No sé qué quiere), and exclamations (¡Qué bonito!). Without the accent, these words usually connect parts of a sentence instead: el libro que quiero means “the book that I want.”
cards.questionEn: Why do words such as que, como, and cuando sometimes have a written accent?
How can you say that some amount or item is still left?
cards.answerEn: Use quedar with the thing or amount that remains: queda for one thing and quedan for more than one.
cards.noteEn: The remaining thing controls the verb. Use queda with a singular or uncounted thing, as in queda café, and quedan with plural things, as in quedan dos entradas.
Te can mean “to you” when you are the recipient or the person affected by an action. It normally appears before a conjugated verb.
With a short indirect word such as me, te, le, nos, or les, quedar can say what someone has left. The plural remaining thing controls quedan; one remaining thing uses queda.
